## Reconnaissance

or provider code changes.

### AUTH-007: Boot through auth state and log on

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. The app root boots through
`GET /auth/state` with a retrying boot screen. Requests send the session
cookie. The logon screen logs on through the account tile with the `duck`
picture. The browser suite signs in through a real session cookie, and
`logon.browser.ts` covers the keyboard path against the real gate.

**Goal**: The web app sends its session cookie, boots by asking
`GET /auth/state`, and a browser without a session can log on and reach the
desktop.

**Scope**:

- `apiRequest` sends `credentials: "include"`; `ApiError` gains `status`.
- `apps/web/src/app.tsx`: owns the boot screen's minimum duration, reads
  `GET /auth/state`, and shows the boot screen, a setup placeholder, the logon
  screen, or `DesktopShell`. `main.tsx` renders it.
- `DesktopShell` drops its boot sequence and keeps the `/health` tray poll.
- Boot screen failure state: `kraziTV can't reach its server.`, **Retry**, and
  an automatic retry every 10 seconds.
- `apps/web/src/logon/`: the logon screen's background, branding, and one user
  tile showing the display name and the `duck` drawing; click or Enter expands
  it to a password box and green arrow; focus moves to the box; the box and
  button disable while the request runs; `invalid_password` shows the balloon
  tip and clears the box; success shows the desktop shell.
- The `duck` avatar drawing in `branding/avatars/`, so the tile has a picture.
- The lower-right Account Settings hint.
- The browser suite reaches the desktop again: create the account and a
  session through `AuthService` and add the cookie to the Playwright context.

**Out of scope**: The setup screen's form (AUTH-008), the throttle countdown
(AUTH-009), `401` handling on the desktop (AUTH-010), Log Off (AUTH-011), and
the other avatars (AUTH-012). Until AUTH-008, `setupRequired` shows a
placeholder that says to finish setup.

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-001 through AUTH-004 (complete).

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer (the project has no dedicated web role).
- The app root is the auth state holder the later tickets extend. Keep it a
  small state machine over the four screens, not a context provider, until a
  second consumer needs it.
- Show the login's `401` answer on the logon screen; do not route it anywhere.
- Original CSS gradient and highlight lines only; no Microsoft artwork, logos,
  or fonts.
- `injectBrowserApi` forwards `request.headers()`, which in Playwright leaves
  out the `cookie` header. Switch it to `await request.allHeaders()`, or the
  context cookie never reaches `GET /auth/state` and the suite stops at the
  logon screen.

**Verification**:

- jsdom app-root tests with `BrowserApi`: authenticated state opens the
  desktop; unauthenticated state shows the tile with the display name; a
  failed `/auth/state` shows the message and **Retry**, and **Retry** with a
  now-working reply opens the right screen.
- jsdom logon tests: Tab reaches the tile, Enter opens it and focuses the box,
  Enter submits; a held login disables the box and button; `invalid_password`
  shows the balloon tip, clears the box, and keeps the screen; a successful
  login shows the desktop.
- An `apiRequest` test proves `credentials: "include"` and `status` on
  `ApiError`.
- `npm run test:browser` passes against the gated test server.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### AUTH-008: Set up the account on first run

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. The setup screen replaces the placeholder. It checks
the name and passwords before sending, and opens the desktop on success. A
`409` re-reads the auth state and shows the logon screen. A browser test
covers first-run setup against the real gate.

**Goal**: A fresh install shows the setup screen, and completing it opens the
desktop.

**Scope**:

- Setup screen in `logon/`: the same background, one `Welcome to kraziTV`
  panel, **Your name**, **Password**, **Confirm password**, and **Next**.
- Client checks: name 1–40 characters after trimming, password 8–256
  characters, both passwords match. Server `invalid_request` messages still
  show.
- **Next** calls `POST /auth/setup` and shows the desktop on success.
- `409 already_set_up` re-reads `GET /auth/state` and shows the logon screen.
- Replaces AUTH-007's placeholder.

**Out of scope**: Choosing an avatar; the new account gets `duck`.

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-007.

**Implementation notes**: Reuse `controls/form-text.ts` and the existing form
patterns before adding field helpers.

**Verification**:

- jsdom tests: `setupRequired` shows the panel; a 41-character name, a short
  password, and mismatched passwords each block the request and say why; a
  valid form sends the trimmed name and opens the desktop; a `409` reply
  shows the logon screen with the account from the second state read.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### AUTH-009: Count down a throttled logon

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. A `too_many_attempts` answer shows a balloon tip
that counts `retryAfterSeconds` down each second and keeps the box disabled
until zero. A throttle with no usable wait shows the server's message instead.

**Goal**: After too many wrong passwords, the logon screen tells the owner how
long to wait and blocks entry until then.

**Scope**:

- `too_many_attempts` shows a balloon tip with the remaining wait from
  `retryAfterSeconds`, counts it down each second, and disables the box and
  button until it reaches zero.

**Out of scope**: Server throttle behavior (AUTH-003).

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-007.

**Implementation notes**: Read the wait from `ApiError.details`, which already
keeps the envelope's fields. Clear the timer on unmount.

**Verification**:

- jsdom test with fake timers: a `429` reply with `retryAfterSeconds: 3` shows
  3, then 2, then 1, keeps the box disabled, and re-enables it at zero.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### AUTH-010: Leave the desktop on a 401

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. `apiRequest` reports each `401` from a request that
was not aborted to one listener. The app root registers it only while the
desktop shows. One `401` closes every program and re-reads the auth state
once; later `401`s are ignored. The scan cancel request now aborts when its
dialog closes, so its late answer can't end a newer session.

**Goal**: When the session ends while the desktop is open, the app closes
every program and shows the screen `GET /auth/state` names.

**Scope**:

- `apiRequest` reports each `401` to one listener the app root registers.
- While the desktop shell is showing, a reported `401` unmounts it, re-reads
  `GET /auth/state`, and shows the logon screen, or the setup screen if the
  account no longer exists.
- On the logon and setup screens, reported `401`s are ignored; those screens
  handle their own answers.

**Out of scope**: Inactivity locking (the spec's open question).

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-007. AUTH-008 for the setup branch.

**Implementation notes**:

- Several programs can fail at once; a `401` while already leaving the
  desktop does nothing more.
- Programs keep handling their own non-`401` errors. Unmounting aborts their
  in-flight reads through `useResource`'s controllers.

**Verification**:

- jsdom test: with a program open, a gated read answering `401
unauthenticated` closes the window and shows the logon screen; two
  simultaneous `401`s read `/auth/state` once.
- jsdom test: a `401` whose state read says `setupRequired` shows the setup
  screen.
- jsdom test: a wrong password on the logon screen does not trigger the
  listener path.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### AUTH-011: Log off from Start

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. **Log Off** at the bottom of the Start menu opens a
`Log Off kraziTV` confirmation, modal over the inert desktop. Logging off
calls `POST /auth/logout` and shows the logon screen. A failed logout keeps
the desktop open and shows the connection message.

**Goal**: The owner can end their session from the Start menu.

**Scope**:

- **Log Off** at the bottom of the Start menu opens a `Log Off kraziTV`
  confirmation centered over the whole desktop, with **Log Off** and
  **Cancel**.
- **Log Off** calls `POST /auth/logout` and shows the logon screen.
- A failed request keeps the confirmation and desktop open and shows
  `kraziTV couldn't log off. Check the connection and try again.`
- Update the Start menu and boot screen comments that promise no
  authentication actions.

**Out of scope**: Switching users and **Turn off**.

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-007.

**Implementation notes**:

- The confirmation belongs to the desktop shell, not a program window, so it
  is not a `WindowDialog`. Escape and **Cancel** close it; focus starts on
  **Log Off** and returns to Start on cancel.

**Verification**:

- jsdom tests: Log Off sends `POST /auth/logout` and shows the logon screen;
  **Cancel** changes nothing; a failed logout keeps the desktop and shows the
  message.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### AUTH-012: Draw the built-in avatars

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-08. All eight built-in avatars are original SVG drawings
in `branding/avatars/drawings/`, listed in order with `duck` first. An unknown
ID draws `duck`. The picker and server-side ID validation remain with spec 0003.

**Goal**: The web app has every built-in avatar the spec names, ready for the
logon screen and Account Settings.

**Scope**:

- Drawings for `crt-tv`, `antenna`, `remote`, `film-reel`, `popcorn`,
  `guitar`, and `chess` beside AUTH-007's `duck`, in the program icons'
  dimensional style inside an XP user-picture frame.
- One ordered avatar ID list in the web app with `duck` first.
- An `avatarId` without a drawing renders `duck`.

**Out of scope**: The picker and server-side ID validation (spec 0003).

**Blocking dependencies**: AUTH-007.

**Implementation notes**: Reuse `icon-gradients.tsx`. Memoize the avatar
component like `ProgramIcon` if it renders in more than one place.

**Verification**:

- Unit test: every ID in the list renders a drawing; an unknown ID renders the
  `duck` drawing.
- Manual look at the logon screen with each avatar ID.

**Docs impact**: Mark
[spec 0002](../../specs/features/003-auth/specs/0002-logon-screen.md)
`Status: Implemented` if this is the last ticket to close.
